summary.text: A 15-year-old girl was brought to the emergency room with vomiting and loss of consciousness lasting 3 hours after attempting suicide by taking five pills of propafenone (1.5 g) 3 hours before admission. On admission her blood pressure was 70/45 mmHg, heart rate 60/minute and temperature 36.8 °C, and she had a generalized tonic-clonic convulsion treated with midazolam infusion.

The initial ECG showed sinus rhythm, an absent P-wave and an extremely prolonged QRS interval of 280 ms. Arterial blood gas analysis showed mild metabolic acidosis, while blood glucose, electrolytes, hepatic and kidney function tests, troponin 1 and bedside echocardiography were normal. A following ECG showed Brugada phenocopy in leads V1 through V3.

Intravenous sodium bicarbonate, saline and positive inotropic agent infusions were started immediately. Haemodynamic and neurologic findings recovered 4 hours after treatment and, when the acidosis was treated, the ECG abnormalities returned to normal. Holter ECG recording after treatment was normal, and she was discharged without sequel 2 days after admission.

The ajmaline challenge test was negative 2 weeks after the incident, and the Brugada-like pattern was not recognized on surface and 24-hour Holter electrocardiography at follow-up. She had no medication or arrhythmic syncope in the history, and her family members had neither pathological ECG findings nor a history of sudden cardiac death.
